They departed the capital of Kiribati on Wednesday to begin the 830-mile journey to Nikumaroro, which is also part of the multi-island country. The trip comes after a major migration crisis at the Ceuta border in July and as the long-running dispute between Spain and Morocco over the two cities on the North African coast remains unresolved. Spain considers Ceuta and Melilla part of its territory, while Morocco regards both cities and several smaller Spanish-held territories in North Africa as part of its own territory. The city that sits on the southern side of the Strait of Gibraltar also has different names in Spanish and Arabic. In Spain, it is Ceuta. In Arabic, it is Sabta, commonly written as Sebta in Latin script. So why does the same city have two names? And how did a city on the North African coast come under Spanish sovereignty? The name is much older than either modern Spain or Morocco. The city was known as Sabta in Arabic. Spain’s Ministry of Culture identifies Sabta with present-day Ceuta and traces its history through successive periods of Idrisid, Umayyad, Taifa, Almoravid, Almohad and Marinid rule. The Spanish form, Ceuta, developed from earlier forms of the name. Sabta and Ceuta are different linguistic forms of the same city. full_text: Trump’s remarks about new leader in Ukraine come as surprise to Kiev — German journalist According Bild deputy editor-in-chief Paul Ronzheimer, "Zelensky’s advisers are shocked and speechless over the news from Washington" BERLIN, October 11. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump’s statements that Ukraine needs a new leader came as a surprise to Vladimir Zelensky’s inner circle and have led to growing concern among them, Bild deputy editor-in-chief Paul Ronzheimer said on his X page. According to the reporter, "Zelensky’s advisers are shocked and speechless over the news from Washington." "We understood that during the campaign leading up to the midterm elections [for the US Congress], attention would once again be focused on us. But we weren’t prepared for this," a close adviser to Zelensky told Ronzheimer. The journalist noted that the main concern in Kiev is the prospect of Washington completely halting cooperation between intelligence agencies. Earlier, US President Donald Trump told reporters that Zelensky could have ended the conflict with Russia many times, but he prefers not to. He also opined that it is time for Ukraine to change its president. The US president added that he would advise Ukraine to find "a new leader who can make a deal.".

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said the phenomenon would likely bring above-average temperatures to much of the world and alter rainfall patterns, raising the risk of droughts and floods in different regions. Spending at US retailers fell in March as consumers pulled back after the banking crisis fueled recession fears. Retail sales, which are adjusted for seasonality but not for inflation, fell by 1% in March from the prior month, the Commerce Department reported on Friday. That was steeper than an expected 0.4% decline, according to Refinitiv, and above the revised 0.2% decline in the prior month. Investors chalk up some of the weakness to a lack of tax returns and concerns about a slowing labor market. The IRS issued $84 billion in tax refunds this March, about $25 billion less than they issued in March of 2022, according to BofA analysts. That led consumers to pull back in spending at department stores and on durable goods, such as appliances and furniture. Spending at general merchandise stores fell 3% in March from the prior month and spending at gas stations declined 5.5% during the same period. Excluding gas station sales, retail spending retreated 0.6% in March from February. However, retail spending rose 2.9% year-over-year. Smaller tax returns likely played a role in last month’s decline in retail sales, along with the expiration of enhanced food assistance benefits, economists say. “March is a really important month for refunds.
